findings.description: API key stored as plain String instead of SecureString. The ElevenLabsScribeBackend stores the API key as a plain String property, which leaves it vulnerable to memory dumps and crash reports.
findings.fix_recommendation: Replace with SecureString type: 'private let secureAPIKey: SecureString'. Update the initializer to wrap the incoming String in SecureString immediately. Use withSecureAccess pattern when accessing the key for API calls.
findings.cwe: CWE-312: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information

findings.description: Initializer accepts API key as plain String parameter without immediate wrapping in SecureString. This allows the plain key to exist in memory longer than necessary.
findings.code_snippet:
init(apiKey: String, customVocabulary: String = "", removeFillerWords: Bool = false) {
        self.apiKey = apiKey
findings.fix_recommendation: Change parameter to SecureString or wrap immediately: 'self.secureAPIKey = SecureString(apiKey)'. Follow the pattern used in AssemblyAIBackend.swift.
findings.cwe: CWE-312: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information

findings.description: Force unwrapped URL construction for API endpoint. Using force unwrap (!) on URL creation can cause runtime crashes if the URL string is malformed. While this is a hardcoded string, it violates safe coding practices.
findings.fix_recommendation: Use URLComponents or at least guard-let with proper error handling. Consider: 'guard let url = URL(string: "https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/voices") else { throw CloudASRError.invalidUploadURL }'

findings.description: Force unwrapped URL construction for speech-to-text API endpoint. Runtime crash risk if URL construction fails.
findings.fix_recommendation: Use SecureURLConstruction pattern from AssemblyAIBackend.swift or guard-let with proper error handling.

findings.description: Multiple force unwrapped Data conversions in multipart form construction. String.data(using: .utf8) returns optional Data, but code force unwraps with !. While UTF-8 encoding of ASCII strings rarely fails, this is unsafe practice.
findings.fix_recommendation: Replace all force unwraps with guard-let or use a safe helper: 'guard let data = value.data(using: .utf8) else { throw EncodingError.failed }'

findings.description: Force unwrapped URLs in CloudProvider.defaultEndpoint computed property. While these are hardcoded valid URLs, force unwrap creates unnecessary crash risk and sets a bad example for pattern following.
findings.fix_recommendation: Store URLs as static constants computed once, or use guard-let: 'static let assemblyAIEndpoint: URL = { guard let url = URL(string: "...") else { fatalError("Invalid URL") }; return url }()'

findings.description: Force unwrapped Data conversion for newline character in file writing. Minimal risk as newline is valid ASCII.
findings.fix_recommendation: Use safe unwrap or pre-computed constant: 'let newlineData = "\n".data(using: .utf8) ?? Data()'

findings.description: Force unwrapped static URLs in wizard view for external links. These are hardcoded documentation/provider URLs, but should still use safe patterns.
findings.fix_recommendation: Use computed static properties with proper validation or use Link views with string URLs which handle the conversion safely.

recommendations.title: Migrate ElevenLabsScribeBackend to SecureString
recommendations.description: ElevenLabsScribeBackend should follow the security pattern established in AssemblyAIBackend.swift. Replace 'private let apiKey: String' with 'private let secureAPIKey: SecureString' and update all access points to use withSecureAccess pattern.

recommendations.title: Eliminate URL Force Unwraps
recommendations.description: Replace all force unwrapped URL constructions with proper guard-let error handling or use SecureURLConstruction pattern. Priority focus on ElevenLabsScribeBackend.swift and CloudTranscriptionConfiguration.swift.

recommendations.title: Safe Data Conversion Pattern
recommendations.description: Establish a project-wide rule to never use .data(using: .utf8)!. Create a String extension that provides a safe conversion with throw-on-failure semantics.

recommendations.title: Security Audit nonisolated(unsafe) Usage
recommendations.description: While nonisolated(unsafe) is used appropriately for SwiftUI @ObservationIgnored backing storage, ensure no sensitive data (API keys) is stored in these properties. SettingsStore.swift stores API keys in these properties - consider using SecureString there as well.

positive_security_patterns_found.description: Properly uses SecureString for API key storage with withSecureAccess pattern
Comprehensive URL construction with path traversal prevention and domain validation
SecureString implementation with XOR obfuscation, zero-on-deinit, and ~Copyable semantics
Uses SecureURLConstruction for all API endpoint URLs, preventing injection attacks
